newsitem.title: THAILAND: Rescue fund to start investing in Thai bourse.
newsitem.headline: Rescue fund to start investing in Thai bourse.

text.p: A 15.7-billion-baht private rescue fund set up by Thai banks and brokerages would start investing in battered Thai stocks from Friday, Olarn Chaipravat, president of the Thai Bankers Association, said.

Olarn announced the fund's decision to enter the market after meeting bankers and government officials in charge of the Thai equities sector in the wake of sharp losses suffered by the domestic bourse since late August.
Sirin Nimmanahaeminda, chief executive of state-owned Krung Thai Bank Plc, confirmed Olarn's statement that the rescue fund would start buying Thai stocks on Friday.
The SET index lost about 10 percent in the past eight sessions to end Friday morning near a three-year low of 999.55 points.
But the market stabilised soon after the news of the rescue fund move.
At 0807 GMT, the index was down 14.82 points, or 1.45 percent, at 1,007.86, hanging above the psychologicaly-important 1,000-point.
Sirin said Krung Thai Bank was prepared to provide at least a 700 million-baht advance immediately, part of a five billion-baht pool being contributed by banks to buy shares on Friday.

Thai brokers and sub-brokers have pledged to chip in the remaining 10.5 billion baht to help shore up the market, which has tumbled sharply this week, partly also due to negative sentiment that accompanied a decision by Moody's Investors Service to downgrade Thailand's short-term debt ratings.
